text:
**For a full recharge in one sunny day, plan on about 300-350 W of panels. A 200 W panel will do it in roughly 1.5 days.**

**The formula** (from [Power Runtime](https://power-runtime.pages.dev/guides/solar-charging/) and [Enough Watts](https://enoughwatts.com/guides/how-much-solar-to-recharge)):

Panel watts ≈ capacity ÷ (peak sun hours × ~0.7-0.75)

Panels rarely deliver their rated watts. Heat, sun angle and charge-controller losses cut real output to about 70-75% of the label.

**For a 1,000 Wh station, from empty to full in one day:**

| Peak sun hours | Panel watts needed |
|---|---|
| 3 (cloudy or shoulder season) | ~450 W |
| 4 (typical) | ~340 W |
| 5 (good summer) | ~270 W |
| 6 (Southwest summer) | ~230 W |

Source: [Power Runtime](https://power-runtime.pages.dev/guides/solar-charging/). [Held in Reserve](https://www.heldinreserve.com/power/solar-panels-recharge-power-station/) estimates about 300 W in summer and 700 W or more in a northern winter.

**If you'd rather take longer:**
- A 200 W panel at 4.5 sun hours and 70% efficiency yields about 630 Wh per day, so about 1.5 days ([Power Preflight](https://powerpreflight.com/guides/solar-panel-sizing-portable-power-stations/)).
- A 100 W panel takes about 3 days.
- A 400 W panel takes under a day, if your station can accept that much.

**Check before you buy:**
- **Maximum solar input watts.** Many 1,000 Wh stations cap at 200-800 W. Panels beyond the cap add nothing.
- **Input voltage range.** The panel's open-circuit voltage (Voc) must stay inside your station's window. Going over can damage it. Be extra careful when wiring panels in series.
- **Loads.** If you run devices while charging, subtract their draw from the solar input.

**One option if your station takes 400 W:** the [ALLPOWERS SP037 400 W foldable panel](https://dealectric.com/go/allpowers-sp037-400w-solar-panel) is listed at $299, or $269.10 with code ALLPOWERS26 (per [Dealectric](https://dealectric.com/allpowers-sp037-400w-solar-panel)). That link is an affiliate link, so Dealectric earns a commission at no cost to you. Its Voc is 45.3 V, so it won't suit stations limited to 24-28 V inputs. It also weighs 18.5 kg (about 41 lb), which is heavy for a portable panel. If your station tops out at 200-300 W, a smaller panel is the better buy.
